title: In vivo Structural Assessments of Ocular Disease in Rodent Models using Optical Coherence Tomography
protocol: Set up the optical coherence tomography equipment.
Open the SD-OCT software.
Define who is taking the OCT, the study, and the treatment arm.
Name these categories in a way that will help researchers search for the desired scans later during data analysis.
Click Test Examiner in the Patient/Exam tab to select the examiner name.
Use the Setup Examiners & Physicians button to add new examiners.
Define the study by clicking Study Name.
Add a new study or modify treatments in an existing study by clicking the Study tab.
Select a treatment arm by clicking to the right of Select Treatment Arm.
Add a new timepoint for an entire group by clicking the Add Patient button.
Enter ID number, First name, and Last name in the window that appears.
Select Male or Female gender.
Enter the Date of Birth.
Click the Add Exam button to add individual rats.
Identify the rats by clicking on an exam.
Edit Exam and enter the ID number into the Enter Notes box.
Click the Save Changes button.
Attach the proper lens to the device as specified for the animal species and region of eye being imaged.
Select the corresponding Configuration in the software.
Dial in the associated reference arm position manually if available.
Double-click the highlighted exam in the Patient/Exam tab to proceed to the Imaging tab.
Delete any default scan by right clicking on it.
Load a pre-set Scan Protocol by clicking the Select a protocol from the list button.
Alternatively, add individual scans as needed for specific imaging requirements.
Anesthetize rats with ketamine (60 mg/kg) and xylazine (7.5 mg/kg) via intraperitoneal injection.
Anesthetize mice with ketamine (80 mg/kg) and xylazine (16 mg/kg) via intraperitoneal injection.
Wait until animals are fully anesthetized and do not respond to toe pinch.
Administer pupil dilation drops (1% tropicamide).
Wait for pupils to dilate before imaging.
Provide thermal support.
Place the rodent in a rodent alignment system that can rotate the animal in 3-dimensional space.
Apply liquid to keep the eyes lubricated.
Ensure the opposite eye is also kept moist during imaging.
Wick away excess saline just before imaging using a delicate task wipe.
Position the animal using the rodent alignment system for horizontal gaze.
Use OCT in Free Run mode to orient the retina for data collection.
Move the scan head closer to the eye until the retina is visible.
Adjust the animal position up/down using the rodent alignment system.
Swivel/twist the animal to position the optic nerve head in the center.
Make the horizontal scan horizontal and the vertical scan vertical.
Adjust the working distance such that the retinal image is flat.
Adjust the reference arm position to keep the image near the top of the display window.
Define a volume scan consisting of 1000 x 100 x 1 for averaging in glaucoma, retinal degeneration, and diabetic retinopathy models.
Take a 3 x 3 mm volume scan in rats.
Take a 1.5 x 1.5 mm volume scan in mice.
Center the optic nerve in the horizontal and vertical access.
Ensure the volume scan is centered with the optic nerve head at the center.
Scan and re-center to make sure it is exactly in the center.
Repeat the scan until the optic nerve head is centered along both axes.
Click the Snapshot button to take a photo.
Flatten and center the images when taking direct thickness measurements through retinal layers to improve accuracy along the anterior-posterior direction.
Take a radial scan centered at the optic nerve head that is 1000 x 4 x 20 (A-scan x B-scan x repeated B-scans).
Use repeated B scans to enhance image clarity of the eye or retina.
Save the image.
Repeat steps for contralateral eye.
Center the middle of the eye and retina in the field of view.
Take three radial scans (whole eye scans): a linear B scan that is 1000 x 5 x 2 and two additional linear B scans of 1000 x 5 x 2 at the same location.
Save the images.
Store saved data on a cloud for good data management and easy access.
Perform data analysis using custom software developed in a mathematical modeling program.
Remove the rodent from the alignment system after imaging.
Inject atipamezole intraperitoneally (1 mg/kg) to reverse xylazine effects, allowing faster recovery.
Place the rodent on a heating pad for recovery.
Give additional saline drops as needed during recovery.
Return rodents to their home cage once they regain full ambulation.
Close the program and turn off the OCT system.
Process OCT images using custom software developed in a mathematical modeling program.
Use specific programs depending on the image purpose (mouse retina, rat retina, or myopia/axial length).
Select OCT scans for processing.
Define the center of the optic nerve head by clicking on it.
Observe the program generating vertical lines at specified distances from the optic nerve head center.
Delineate retinal layers along each line: RNFL, IPL, INL, OPL, ONL, ELM, IS/OS, RPE, and total retinal thickness.
Export measurements into a spreadsheet software for data analysis.
Determine differences in nasal-temporal and inferior-superior axis at 0.5 mm and 1.2 mm distances for retinal measurements.
Open the mathematical modeling program.
Select an image to load.
Manually mark each scan (radial and B scans).
Mark the anterior and posterior edges of the cornea, lens, vitreous chamber, and retina.
Exit the program after marking.
Save delineated values in a spreadsheet software.
Average three separate scans together.
